approach: Add `check_design_existing_code(reading: &Reading) -> Result<()>` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, modelled on `check_code_survey`. It applies when class_of_work is "design", a capability is set and there is no question. It refuses unless (a) an assumption whose trimmed text starts `Existing code:` (any case) names a `crates/` or `docs/` path, and (b) some criterion mentions both "existing code" and "section". It is wired as `step!(check_design_existing_code(reading));` right after `check_code_survey` in `refusing_check`. It reads only the reading: no model call, no repository search. The refusal text names the missing `Existing code:` assumption and says to list modules, clients, fakes, tests and doc sections with paths, plus a criterion that the doc carries an Existing code section stating reuse, extend or new per proposed component. The rule is taught by that refusal, so the reader prompt does not grow. Tests: unit tests in reading.rs; three new refusal-corpus cases (two refused by the new check, one accepted) and one new input-form tag; a CHANGELOG entry; briefs.rs gets a doc-comment-only edit, so prompt text and token budgets are unchanged. Input forms the rule handles: a design reading with no assumptions; an `Existing code:` assumption with no repo path; the label not at the start of an assumption; label in other case or with leading spaces; an assumption but no 'existing code ... section' criterion; both present; non-design classes; design with a question or a decline. Corpus mapping is in the demonstration for criterion 2 (existing ids read: code-reading-without-a-survey, code-reading-with-a-survey, crate-relative-deliverable-path; the three new ids are added by plan step 4).

decisions.choice: Enforce the rule as a deterministic reading-gate check in refusing_check, on the reading's own assumptions and criteria.
decisions.reason: The fault starts where a design reading is accepted from the request text alone, with no inventory of existing code. `refusing_check` is the one gate every reading passes, and the corpus guard forces a refusing case for each new `step!`. One check covers every design job, not the Jev one.

rejected.option: Search the repository snapshot for components the doc names and compare them with the reading
rejected.why: Out of scope (no model call or repository search in the reader); needs fragile entity extraction. `check_code_survey` reads only the reading.

rejected.option: Edit the Jev design docs, decisions.md or earlier CHANGELOG work
rejected.why: That work landed and is out of scope. The fix is prevention at the gate.

rejected.option: Add a producer-side or verifier-side step
rejected.why: It would catch the problem after the reading is accepted, which is the late detection being removed.

decisions.choice: Recognise a survey by the label `Existing code:` at the start of an assumption (trim, case-insensitive) naming a `crates/` or `docs/` path followed by an alphanumeric character; recognise the criterion by the words 'existing code' and 'section', any kind.
decisions.reason: Mirrors `code_surveys` and `names_crates_path`; a bare `crates/` or prose with no path does not pass. Design docs live under docs/, so docs/ counts. The error text can teach the exact phrasing.

rejected.why: A design for a docs-only area could not satisfy it.
The Existing code section is doc content, a content criterion; Behavior would push the reader to invent a command.

decisions.choice: Teach the rule through the refusal message; change only a doc comment in briefs.rs.
decisions.reason: The reader prompt is 1997 of 2000 tokens; `the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line` asserts 5 rule lines.

rejected.why: Breaks the 5-line assertion and the token budget.

rejected.option: Shorten other prompt text to make room
rejected.why: Out of scope and risks tests that pin that text.

decisions.choice: Place the new `step!` after `check_code_survey` and before `check_governance_coverage`.
decisions.reason: It sits beside the other survey rule, and runs before boundary and path checks so the survey correction is not delayed a round trip.

rejected.why: A reading with a bad path would be told about paths first and the survey in a second round trip.

decisions.choice: Declare the intended refusal in a doc comment, the CHANGELOG and a unit test ('expected 5% of newly refused readings', labelled an estimate).
decisions.reason: The replay (`replay_declaration`, `declared_percent`) holds a job that newly refuses more than 10% unless a share is declared. Follows `code_survey_refusal_is_declared_intended`.

rejected.why: The replay could hold the job and criterion 4 asks for the declared share.

risks.risk: Existing tests or fixtures that build a design-class reading with a capability through the gate would now be refused.

risks.risk: The new step confuses the corpus step-name extractor or `function_body`.
risks.mitigation: Use the plain form `step!(check_design_existing_code(reading));` inside `refusing_check` and keep no lone `}` line before the function end.

risks.risk: A refusing corpus case is refused by an earlier check, so the expected check name differs.
risks.mitigation: Build each case from `base_reading`, change only class_of_work, assumptions and criteria, use only paths in `repo_files()`, and avoid producer-report words in criteria.

risks.risk: The replay of accepted readings holds the job for refusing more than 10%.
risks.mitigation: Criteria and CHANGELOG declare 'expected 5% of newly refused readings'; a unit test asserts the share parses to Some(5).

risks.risk: A refused reader still cannot satisfy the rule and fails twice.
risks.mitigation: The message gives the exact label, path prefixes and criterion wording, as `check_code_survey` does.
Keep it behaving identically (wrapper over a shared scan or a separate helper); existing code_survey_* tests still run.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in the `tests` module of reading.rs drive `check_reading_acceptance` through the existing `accept` helper and call `check_design_existing_code` directly on constructed readings. Cases: (a) no assumptions -> Err containing `Existing code:`, `crates/`, `docs/`; (b) `Existing code:` with no path or `Existing code: crates/ was read` -> Err; (c) assumption naming docs/design/jev-code-health.md and crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs but no 'existing code ... section' criterion -> Err; (d) both present -> Ok; (e) label in other case with leading spaces -> Ok; (f) label not at the start -> Err.
demonstrations.observes: (a), (b), (c), (f) return the refusal and (d), (e) are accepted, through the real gate with no fake.
demonstrations.fails_without: The refusal asserts in (a), (b), (c), (f) fail if `check_design_existing_code` is absent or not wired into `refusing_check`, because the reading is accepted; without the change the test module does not compile.

Fixture: existing `scoped_reading` and `accept` helpers (exist; read); step 3 adds `design_reading(assumptions, criteria)` built from `scoped_reading`. No double.

Add 'design-existing-code' to INPUT_FORMS (15 -> 16). Each case is built from `base_reading` changing only class_of_work, assumptions and criteria, using paths in `repo_files()`.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `design_existing_code_does_not_apply_outside_its_gate`, modelled on `code_survey_does_not_apply_outside_its_gate`: start from a design reading that would be refused, change one field. Classes code, tests, docs, config with no `Existing code:` assumption -> Ok; capability None with decline_reason -> Ok; question Some -> Ok. Docs, config and question readings also go through `accept`. The unchanged design reading is asserted refused in the same test.
demonstrations.observes: All non-design readings and design readings with a question or decline are accepted by the new check, while the plain design reading is refused, showing the rule is class-wide and gated, not a one-job check.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the check ignored class_of_work, the question guard or the decline guard, the loop over non-design readings would return Err and the test fails; if the check were absent, the design-refused assertion fails.
